classification.difficultyReason: Reverse a four-stage probability calculation without replacement to determine the remaining deck size.

content.prompt: A number of cards are to be taken out of a standard 52-card deck. The resultant deck contains all four aces. If four cards are selected without replacement, then the probability of selecting all aces is $\frac{1}{1001}$. How many cards had been taken out of the original deck?

answer.short:
38 cards.

Multiply the successive probabilities of drawing the four aces to find that 14 cards remain.
answer.worked:
Let $n$ be the number of cards remaining. Drawing without replacement gives
$$\begin{align*}\Pr(\text{all four aces})&=\frac{4}{n}\times\frac{3}{n-1}\times\frac{2}{n-2}\times\frac{1}{n-3}\\\Pr(\text{all four aces})&=\frac{24}{n(n-1)(n-2)(n-3)}.\end{align*}$$
Hence
$$\begin{align*}n(n-1)(n-2)(n-3)&=24\times1001\\n(n-1)(n-2)(n-3)&=24024.\end{align*}$$
Since $14\times13\times12\times11=24024$, there are 14 cards remaining. The product increases with integer $n\ge4$, so this is the only possible deck size.
$$\text{Cards removed}=52-14=38.$$
